h1: TFF Membrane Area and Flux Calculator
summary:
A tangential-flow filtration step is sized by the volume to process and the flux the membrane will hold, and the membrane area then fixes how long the step takes. It returns membrane area required, cassettes to install, diafiltration buffer needed and estimated step time, and the panel shows all of them at once.

This calculator returns the area, the number of cassettes, the diafiltration volume and the step time at your flux. Every result is derived from the boxes you fill in, so changing one input updates the whole panel at once. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the TFF Membrane Area and Flux
sections.html:
Area = max(batch ÷ load capacity, batch ÷ flux-based area); DF buffer = (V ÷ CF) × DV; time ≈ (V + V·DV/CF) ÷ (area × flux)

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
Vstarting batch volumeL
Jpermeate fluxL/m²/h
CFconcentration factor (final ÷ initial volume)×
DVdiafiltration volumes—

sections.title: How do I use the TFF Membrane Area and Flux?
sections.html:
The form asks only for what the formula needs — nothing is optional decoration.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: batch volume of 500 L, permeate flux of 60 L/m²/h, concentration factor of 8 x, diafiltration volumes of 5 DV, area per cassette of 2.5 m², maximum load per m² of 100 L/m².

Substituting them into the formula gives membrane area required of 8.33 m², cassettes to install of 4 cassettes, diafiltration buffer needed of 312.5 L, estimated step time of 2.12 h, area set by the load limit of 5 m², which limit sets the area (1 = flux, 2 = load) of 1.

The arithmetic is the page's own: change one box and the result moves by the amount the formula implies, which is the quickest way to convince yourself the tool is honest.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
A raw figure only means something next to the bands it is normally judged against. Here is the scale that goes with this one:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
30 – 60Conservative fluxhigh-mass, fouling feeds
60 – 100Typicala well-behaved mAb ultrafiltration step
above 100Aggressiveonly with pre-filtered, low-titre streams

  • Flux falls as the feed concentrates, so the time estimate is optimistic unless the quoted flux is the average over the step, not the clean-water value.

  • Diafiltration is done at constant volume: you add buffer at the rate permeate leaves, and the buffer volume needed is (retentate volume) × DV.

  • Install at least one cassette more than the calculation suggests; a single cassette leaves no margin for a fouled membrane.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
The arithmetic is simple; the inputs are where things go wrong. The usual culprits:

  • Using clean-water flux for a cell-culture feed, where fouling cuts it by half or more.
  • Forgetting the hold-up volume of the system and tubing when quoting yield.
  • Sizing exactly to the load limit and then having to dilute the batch to finish the step.

faq.q: How do I choose a cassette size?
faq.a: Round the calculated area up to whole cassettes, then check the retentate channel height gives a sensible crossflow for your pump.
A volume of buffer equal to the current retentate volume; five volumes remove about 99.3% of a freely permeating impurity.

faq.q: What does the TFF Membrane Area and Flux actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns membrane area required, cassettes to install, diafiltration buffer needed and estimated step time. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
